  • I had serious issues to get the correct USB flash drives for a BIOS reflash. The one in the front that can be loaded by the BIOS is not accepted by that BIOS reflash port in the back. I literally have 2 different USB flash drives in order to restore the BIOS.

If you BIOS gets crippled, then you can switch the BIOS switch and start up with the other BIOS. But if you end up in the misery that I have had, then both BIOS will be crippled. You need the emergency back BIOS. In order to make the motherboard accept that one, power off your PC. Then hit that small button on the back. It will automatically power on the PC and start flashing. This is badly explained din the manual, I always assumed that the PC must have been powered on.

Be prepared to have Windows software that broke the DRM, when you reflash and power up Windows 10.
